mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, تلقونَ إِلَيْهِم بالمودة: تلقون is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of أولياء.
His saying يخرجُون الرَّسُول: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in كفروا.
His saying أَن تؤمنوا: أن is in the position of the accusative, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying إِن كُنْتُم خَرجْتُمْ: إنْ is for condition, and the apodosis of the condition is in the preceding speech, because it did not govern [anything] in the wording.
His saying جهادا: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl; it is also said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; like it is وابتغاء مرضاتي.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying يَوْم الْقِيَامَة يفصل بَيْنكُم: يوم is an adverb whose governing word is تنفعكم, and you pause on القيامة. It is also said that يفصل is the governing word in the adverb; then you pause on بينكم and do not pause on القيامة.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying إِنَّا برآء مِنْكُم: it is the plural of بريء, like كريم and كرماء. Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar permitted بِراء with a kasra on the بآء, treating it like كريم and كرام. Al-Farrāʾ permitted بَراء with a fatḥa on the بآء, in the form of the singular indicating the plural, as in His saying, Exalted is He, إنني براء مما تعبدون. براء is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it applies to the singular and the plural in a single form; its precise sense is "I am possessed of disavowal", i.e. possessed of dissociation from you.
His saying أَن تبروهم: أن is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) of الذين, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); like it is أن تولوهم. It is also said that the two are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying إِلَّا قَول إِبْرَاهِيم: قول is an exception not of the same kind as the first (disconnected exception).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t:
His saying مهاجرات: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of المؤمنات.
His saying مؤمنات: the second object of علم, and هنّ is the first.
His saying أَن تنكحوهن: أن is in the position of the accusative by the omission of the preposition, its implied form being "in marrying them" (في أن تنكحوهن), i.e. there is no blame on you in marrying them when you have given them their dues. [Translator's note: the edition prints «تنكحوهم» in the implied form.]
